clue.text: Firm even ruins affair with internal measure

indicators.note: even here means the even-numbered letters, the second and fourth of the word ruins
internal says the measure goes inside the affair, splitting it

parts.note: a fling is a brief love affair
an inch is a unit of length measure

explanation.surface: A firm's books are wrecked by an affair and some internal bookkeeping measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' takes the even letters of 'ruins', not an even-numbered word; 'internal' splits the affair around the measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone firm in the face of danger does not wince or draw back, a straightforward adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Lost the thread and stupidly cued pink

indicators.note: stupidly suggests the letters of cued pink are handled carelessly and jumbled

explanation.surface: A snooker player loses concentration and foolishly strikes the pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' rearranges CUEDPINK.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitching that has been unpicked has had its thread pulled out, so it has literally lost the thread.

clue.text: Where drivers may have top start

definitions.text: Where drivers may have top start

parts.words: Where drivers may have top start
parts.note: in golf a driver is the club for the opening shot, and every round begins at the first hole's teeing ground

clue.text: Infant son Abraham almost ceremonially tops

definitions.text: Infant son Abraham almost ceremonially tops

explanation.surface: The child whom Abraham nearly sacrificed in a ritual on the mountain.

explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the patriarch Abraham's boy was bound on an altar and almost offered up before an angel intervened.

clue.text: Crocodile making a change to it is a banker

explanation.walkthrough: 'making a change to' swaps the A in CAYMAN for IT. A CITY MAN works in the City of London, its financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A man working in the City of London, Britain's financial district, is typically a banker or financier.

a model sits, or poses, for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone asks an alien whether the jelly has set.
explanation.definitionFit: When making jelly the cook asks whether it has firmed up yet, the question being about setting.

clue.text: Large entry from target age range

explanation.walkthrough: 'range' rearranges TARGETAGE. The Great Gate is the grand entrance of Trinity College, Cambridge.

clue.text: Standard reflecting wave of radio ham

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city gives its name to a well-known cured ham, so this is a type of the meat.

clue.text: Goes round unopened craft gardens

indicators.note: round says the attempts surround the other piece

parts.note: a go at something is an attempt, so goes are tries

explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' removes the opening letter of the craft; 'round' wraps the attempts around what is left. The Tuileries are formal gardens in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuileries are the famous formal gardens in central Paris beside the Louvre.

clue.text: Tom first searches Chambers for "dead"

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

clue.text: Dismantled what actor had done

clue.text: Individualist individual lost his head embracing Gaff

explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson, author of the essay Self-Reliance, championed individualism and non-conformity.

clue.text: Nearly turn up with mushrooms for fan

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' cuts ROTATE to ROTAT; 'up' turns the whole of ROTATCEPS into SPECTATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan at a match is someone watching the game, an onlooker.

clue.text: Papist separately boards river, road and rail transport

RC is Roman Catholic, an old slur being papist

clue.text: Purchase of old hot concoction
